security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are JavaScript syntax, fixed example markup, documentation, or expected media processing without shell execution. Three template sinks allow unescaped plan metadata to execute browser scripts, and setup can bypass Python package protections outside the project. No evidence found of credential theft, malicious exfiltration, or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Review templates interpolate plan identifiers, titles, and transcript excerpts into innerHTML.
remediation.suggestion: Build elements with createElement and assign metadata through textContent. Validate timing fields as finite numbers before assigning styles.

remediation.issue: Setup installs NumPy outside the project and falls back to --break-system-packages.
remediation.suggestion: Create a project-local virtual environment, install Python dependencies there, and remove the package-protection bypass.

content.value_statement: Talking-head videos need supporting visuals that match the speaker without hiding important moments. This skill plans, animates, and renders continuous-shape B-roll from footage and transcripts.
actual_capabilities: Inspect video dimensions, frame rate, black frames, and likely picture-in-picture regions using ffprobe, ffmpeg, and NumPy.
Estimate word timestamps from SRT or VTT cues and request approval for a clip plan.
Build self-contained HTML animations with spring-driven shapes, cursor paths, and speech-timed state changes.
Capture contact sheets and render motion-blurred MP4 cutaways or transparent ProRes 4444 MOV panels.
Composite review previews with source audio and generate clip viewers, comparison pages, and timing notes.
limitations: Requires Node 18+, Python 3, ffmpeg, NumPy, Playwright, and Chromium; transparent exports require the prores_ks encoder.
Subtitle-based word times are estimates, and black-region layout detection requires visual review.
Rendering captures four subframes per frame and can be slower than real time; final editing remains manual.
Setup downloads dependencies and may modify shared Python packages; review pages request Google Fonts and currently require trusted plan metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Your First B-Roll
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [video path] and [SRT path]. Propose light B-roll coverage and wait for my approval before building clips.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: choose a few clear visual moments.

prompt_templates.title: Render Approved Cutaways
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the approved cutaways for [video path] using [transcript path]. Match source resolution and frame rate. Check key-word stills before rendering.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: produce full-frame animations from an approved plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design Transparent Panels
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [video path] for picture-in-picture regions. Plan transparent panels using [brand assets]. Keep animations clear of the largest speaker box and request approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: adapt layouts to branded overlays.

prompt_templates.title: Deliver a Complete Review Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [approved plan] and [word timestamps] to render cutaways and transparent panels. Check morphs, export a preview, and generate review pages and timing notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate mixed treatments and editor handoff.

output_examples.input: A product walkthrough with an SRT transcript and light animation coverage.
output: An approval table lists selected moments, spoken lines, animation actions, treatments, and reasons.
A pill expands into a product card, then becomes a comparison control on selected words.
Timeline-named MP4 clips, a composite preview, and timing notes support editor handoff.

output_examples.input: A picture-in-picture tutorial with empty space beside the speaker.
output: A layout report identifies the speaker region and flags detected size or position changes.
A transparent ProRes panel morphs from a folder into a process display without covering the speaker.
A browser-compatible panel preview and synchronized comparison page support visual review.

best_practices: Approve the clip plan first and provide real names, figures, and brand assets before animation begins.
Check contact sheets at important words and mid-morph moments; verify speaker clearance, readability, and cursor position.
Use trusted metadata and a project-local Python environment; review dependency installation before running setup.
anti_patterns: Inventing performance figures, prices, quotes, or results that the transcript and user do not provide.
Covering personal statements or the opening hook with unnecessary full-frame animations.
Opening review pages generated from untrusted plan metadata or running setup blindly on a shared Python installation.

faq.question: What input files should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a local video and preferably an SRT or VTT transcript. Brand colors, logos, and screenshots are optional.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically transcribe audio?
faq.answer: No transcription script is included. The instructions suggest a separate faster-whisper workflow or requesting a timestamped transcript.

faq.question: How accurate is speech timing?
faq.answer: The subtitle parser estimates word times at approximately 0.2-second accuracy. Important animation changes still need visual and audio review.

faq.question: Which export formats are supported?
faq.answer: Full-frame cutaways export as MP4. Transparent panels use ProRes 4444 MOV and require the ffmpeg prores_ks encoder.

faq.question: Does the workflow need network access?
faq.answer: Setup downloads dependencies and Chromium. Review pages load Google Fonts. Local rendering uses the installed tools and source files.

faq.question: Is the composite preview a finished edit?
faq.answer: No. The preview uses hard cuts and source audio. Place the individual clips in your editor for final timing, transitions, and audio mixing.
